get.summary: Determine if changes between two revisions are authorized
get.description:
This API checks for unauthorized changes between any two versions of a firewall policy.
The API returns authorized if and only if all traffic changes between the two versions were authorized by SecureChange tickets.
The API returns unauthorized if there is at least one change that cannot be matched to a SecureChange ticket.

The API checks access that was granted (checked against access requests with action=Accept) as well as access that was removed (checked against access requests with action=Drop or Remove).
The API returns the authorization status, the relevant tickets in SecureChange and the rules that implement unauthorized access changes.

Note 1: To use this API you must enable "Authorize Revisions with Tickets" in SecureTrack/Configuration/Ticketing.
Note 2: Use the ID returned by the /revisions API for new_version and old_version.
Note 3: The default value for traffic_details and ignore_tickets is false.
Note 4: Traffic that is handled by an implicit rule will not have a rule ID.

parameters.name: traffic_details
parameters.description: Return unauthorized traffic change details for all modified rules

parameters.name: ignore_tickets
parameters.description: Ignore SecureChange tickets and consider all traffic changes unauthorized

200.description: Change authorization has been successfully calculated

400.description: Could not find the requested revisions for comparison

post.summary: Compare revisions on two different devices in terms of traffic.
post.description:
This API compares two arbitrary revisions from any devices. The comparison will be done in terms of allowed/denied traffic.
The API returns authorized if and only if there are no differences between the traffic allowed/denied by the rules in the two revisions.
The API returns unauthorized if there is at least one difference in terms of allowed/denied traffic between the two revisions.
Note 1: To map policies from one revision to the other use oldId2newIdMap and provide the UIDs of the policies to be compared.
Note 2: Parameter in the request body specifies if the result will return  traffic difference details for all incompatible rules 
Note 3: The format of the result is the same as the one returned by /change_authorization 
Note 4: The API accepts in request body only one pair of oldId  - newId map 
Note 5: The request is valid only if the mapping ids are found in the active policies

400.description: Could not find the requested revisions for comparison

Use this API to add a single device or a list of devices to SecureTrack. 
The following devices can be added: Check Point CMA R80, SMC R80, Smart 1 Cloud; Cisco ASA; Cisco Router; Cisco Nexus; Cisco XR; Cisco Meraki; Palo Alto Panorama NG; Fortinet FortiManager; Microsoft Azure; Amazon AWS; Arista CVP and EOS 
The API body should include a JSON file with the mandatory parameters for the operation. 
String parameters contain only lower and upper case letters, digits, space, dot, backward slash, forward slash, underscore or one of the following signs: #@:;=!^(). 
Currently supported types: CMA, SMC, Smart 1 Cloud, ASA, Cisco Router, Nexus, XR, Cisco Meraki, Panorama NG, FortiManager, Azure, AWS, Arista CVP and EOS

This API verifies connection to the provided device, before adding a device.
This is done by:
  Cisco - Connect with SSH and see that the credentials are correct.
  Check Point (Excluding  Smart 1 Cloud) - Test OPSEC connectivity. For R80 devices, this also verifies the connectivity for API login.
  Panorama - Login through the API to check connectivity.
  Fortimanager - Login through the API to check connectivity.
  Arista - The SSL certificate is retrieved.
If the connection test fails the device will not be added.
The connection is not verified for Smart 1 Cloud, Cisco Router,Nexus and XR. 
Only "live" device with correct credentials can be added using this API.
For Cisco Router, Nexus and XR there are 2 usage examples : one only with mandatory fields (device name example : Router-Cisco-mandatory-fields) and one with both mandatory and optional fields ( device name example : Router-Cisco-all-fields). 
 Only for Cisco Router, the 'router_operating_system' field can take the following values: IOS, IOS-XE and IOS-XE-SDWAN. The latter corresponds to Cisco Viptela cEdge routers. 

When adding a new AWS or Azure device and the field use_cloud_organization is set to true, than the cloud_organization and account_id or subscription _id fields become mandatory. 
The value for cloud_organization must match the name defined in the Cloud Organization settings within TOS. 
Only users with Super Admin privileges are authorized to use this setting. 
When adding a new Azure subscription using the API, the usage analysis feature will be turned off by default, unless you explicitly specify "collect_rule_usage_traffic_logs" : true and also "collect_object_usage_traffic_logs" : true and also "rule_optimizer_usage" : true.   Cisco - Connect with SSH and see that the credentials are correct.

  Panorama - Login through the API to check connectivity.
  Fortimanager - Login through the API to check connectivity.

2. Device network object name (for example: "netobj:422:net_22.22.22.0" refers to network object named "net_22.22.22.0" related to device with id 422)
3. LDAP Group (for example: "LDAP:cn=grp1:cn=users:dc=tcse:dc=net")
4. NSX security group name (for example: "SG:189:securitygroup-11" refers to a security group named "securitygroup-11", related to NSX root device with id 189)
5. ACI EPG / External EPG / ACI ESG (for example: "EPG:505:TN_ATU_MGMT:ApplicationProfile1:EPG_02", "EXTEPG:505:TN_ATU_MGMT:L3OUT-VRF1:ext_epg1", "ESG:505:TN_ATU_MGMT:ApplicationProfile1:ESG_1")
6. A specific endpoint within ACI External EPG (for example: 30.40.50.60@EXTEPG:505:TN_ATU_MGMT:L3OUT-VRF1:ext_epg1)
7. URL category (destination only, Panorama devices only, for example: UC:my_sport_urls)
8. DNS (for example: DNS:tufin.com)

Service parameter can be "any" or any comma separated combination of the following values:
1. Protocol and port (for example, "tcp:80")
2. A service name (for example: "ftp", "syslog")
3. An application with its default services, case sensitive (for example, "Skype", "Facebook")
4. An application with overridden services, case sensitive (for example, "Skype@tcp:44", "Facebook@(tcp:44,tcp:55)")
5. IP protocol number (for example, "58" for IPv6-ICMP)
If sourceDomainIdTag is provided, the path starting points will be restricted to the specified domain ID.  sourceDomainIdTag is valid only if overlapping IP mode is enabled.
If context is provided, the path will be calculated for the specified domain context, otherwise the default domain context is used. Context is valid only if MSSP mode is enabled.
To get the context, call the /domains/ API and use the ID included within the returned domain DTO.
displayIncompletePaths parameter default value is false, if this parameter is set to true -
all nodes on the path will be displayed, even if the node cannot reach the destination, or if the source and destination are the same.
displayBlockedStatus parameter default value is false, if this parameter is set to true -
blocked traffic icons will be displayed next to devices blocking the traffic.
simulateNat parameter default value is true if this parameter is set to false - NAT simulation will not be used when calculating the path.
lastInstall parameter default value is true, which means simulation would use last installed policies. If this parameter is set to false - simulation would use the last saved policies.
pathIds parameter default value is empty, which means that all paths would be exported to the report.
This API cannot be executed more than 10 times in parallel.

post.summary: Create or update generic Route Maps
post.description:
This API allows creating or updating one or more generic route maps for a specific network device.



	Each route map must contain:

	- A human-readable `name` (unique identifier for the route map)

	- A list of `interfaces` where the route map is applied

	- A list of `entries`, where each entry defines policy-based routing behavior



		Entry Parameters:



		- seq_number: Unique sequence number that defines evaluation order within the route map

		- matcher_policy_name: Name of the generic policy that defines traffic matching criteria

			- Must reference an existing generic policy created via the generic policy APIs

			- See: POST /topology/generic/policy (create policy)

			- See: GET /topology/generic/policy (retrieve policies)

			- The referenced policy contains rules that define source, destination, service, and action criteria

		- entry_action: Action to take when traffic matches the policy ("Accept" or "Deny")

		- actions: Array of routing actions to apply when entry matches and is accepted



		Routing Action Parameters:



		- nexthop: IP address of the next hop router (IPv4/IPv6), e.g. "10.0.0.1""

			- Use null if not setting a specific next hop

		- interface: Name of the egress interface, e.g. "GigabitEthernet0/1", "FastEthernet0/0"

			- Use null if not setting a specific interface

		- vrf: Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) instance name

			- Use null for default/global routing table

		- global_vrf: Boolean flag indicating if the VRF is global (typically false)



	General Notes:

	- The `route_maps` array supports defining multiple independent route maps for the device

	- Route map entries are evaluated sequentially based on `seq_number`

	- At least one routing action (nexthop or interface) should be specified per entry

	- VRF and interface/nexthop combinations enable advanced policy-based routing scenarios

	- The API performs create or update operations based on existing route map configuration

	- All string values are case-sensitive



	Policy Integration:

	- Route maps work in conjunction with generic policies for policy-based routing

	- Generic policies define WHAT traffic to match (source, destination, service criteria)

	- Route maps define WHERE to route that traffic (nexthop, interface, VRF)

	- Workflow: 1) Create generic policies using POST /topology/generic/policy

	           2) Reference those policy names in route map matcher_policy_name fields

	           3) Define routing actions for matched traffic in the route map entries
